purpose: Define Topic-first placement for new specification material: determine all applicable existing Topics first, create additional Topics freely when needed, and keep cross-cutting mechanisms traceable through every affected semantic chain.

topics.name: Topic-Guided Change
topics.purpose: Define Topic-first placement for new specification material: determine all applicable existing Topics first, create additional Topics freely when needed, and keep cross-cutting mechanisms traceable through every affected semantic chain.

operations.name: Place new semantic change by Topic
outputs: existing Topic assignments | new Topic proposal

decision_sequence: resolve all existing Topics it belongs to
if coverage remains semantically incomplete, define a new Topic
compose/inherit existing Topics where that expresses the mechanism
otherwise mark outsider explicitly until resolved
semantics.multi_topic_rule: A mechanism may belong to multiple Topics; e.g. Trigger can be its own Topic and also belong to Core.
semantics.chain_rule: A mechanism such as order creation may be its own Topic and span the entire affected chain.
semantics.local_rule: Topic declarations stay with the nodes/subtrees they classify for recursive readability.
semantics.no_scarcity_rule: Do not reduce Topic count at the cost of semantic clarity.
semantics.documentation_rule: Prefer Topic inheritance/composition over redundant explanatory documents.

invariants.rule: Every machine-significant canonical node is classified by explicit Topic membership or explicitly marked outsider; Topics may inherit and compose other Topics.

hard_gates.condition: change forced into exactly one Topic
new Topic suppressed solely to minimize Topic count
cross-cutting chain effects omitted from Topic membership
Topic stored only in disconnected central directory when local recursive declaration is required
redundant documentation created where Topic composition expresses the mechanism

references.purpose: Cross-cutting mechanisms may compose existing Topics.

prose.summary: Define Topic-first placement for new specification material: determine all applicable existing Topics first, create additional Topics freely when needed, and keep cross-cutting mechanisms traceable through every affected semantic chain.
